title: Avoiding stalemate: one move mates, one draws
description: White is a queen up and Black's king is in the corner. One careless queen move would throw it all away.
prompt: White to move. Finish the game — carefully.
hints: Before you move, check whether Black would still have a legal move.
Qb6 would take away every square without giving check.

notes.1.Qb7#: Checkmate: the queen on b7 is protected by the king and covers a7 and b8.

explanation: Qb6 would be stalemate: Black's king on a8 would have no legal move but wouldn't be in check, and the game would be a draw. Qb7 gives check, the king on c6 protects the queen, and it's checkmate. When you're winning, always ask: does my opponent still have a move?

source.reference: Avoiding stalemate with king and queen (standard endgame technique); verified with Stockfish 19

title: Avoiding stalemate: give the king a square
description: Black's king has no legal move right now. Almost every quiet move White can make is stalemate.
prompt: White to move. Black's king can't move at all. What does that mean for your next move?
hints: If Black had to move now, it would be stalemate.
Every king move would be stalemate. Give Black's king a square back.

notes.1.Qe7: The queen steps back and gives Black's king the square g8 — no stalemate.

explanation: Black's king on h8 has no legal move. Kg6 or Kh6 would be stalemate — in fact every king move would be. First give the king a square with Qe7; after Kg8, Kg6 brings White's king closer and Qf8 is mate. A winning player has to keep the opponent breathing until the very last move.

source.reference: Avoiding stalemate with king and queen (standard endgame technique); verified with Stockfish 19
